title: Rhyming words

parent.learn: Rhyming words end with the same sound: cat, hat, bat.
parent.why: Only the first sound changes; the ending “-at” stays. Hearing that shows the child that words are made of parts.

parent.learn: Change the first sound to make a new word.
parent.why: cat → hat → mat → rat. This is how word families work, and it lets a child read many new words from one they know.

parent.learn: Sing nursery rhymes and stop before the rhyming word.
parent.why: Letting the child fill the gap (“Twinkle, twinkle, little star, how I wonder what you…”) trains the ear to expect the rhyme.

ask: What rhymes with cat? Say as many as you can.
Sing “Twinkle, Twinkle” and stop before the last word of each line.
Make a silly rhyme with your name.
Which word does not rhyme: hen, pen, ten, cup?

rounds.h: bell — well: both end in “-ell”. Ball starts the same but ends differently.
cake and lake both end in “-ake”.

rounds.t: Which word does NOT rhyme with pin?
rounds.h: tin, bin, win all end in “-in”. pan ends in “-an”.

rounds.t: Twinkle, twinkle, little star, how I wonder what you ___
rounds.h: star — are: the rhyme finishes the line.
nest — best: both end in “-est”. net starts the same but ends differently.

rounds.t: Which word is in the same family as man?
rounds.h: man and fan both end in “-an”.

rounds.t: Which one does not rhyme? hen, pen, ten, hat
rounds.h: hen, pen, ten end in “-en”; hat ends in “-at”.
light — kite: both end with the “-ite” sound, even though they are spelt differently.
